items.title: [Bug] Hybrid mamba prefix-cache hit reads out of bounds: add_request seeds the state index with cache_config.block_size after it was lowered below mamba_block_size (Xid 31 / illegal memory access)
items.bodyExcerpt:
**Summary.** `MambaHybridModelState.add_request` seeds the running mamba state slot as
`(num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size`, but by the time it runs, `EngineCore._initialize_kv_caches` has already reassigned `cache_config.block_size` to `min(block_size of prefix-cacheable groups)`. For hybrid models that carry an extra attention group with a small block size (here: a DFlash2/EAGLE-style drafter group with sliding-window spec, block 64 or 1024), that minimum is far below `cache_config.mamba_block_size` (7168 here). The seed therefore indexes the mamba block table in the wrong units, and `precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel` → `_copy_mamba_state_block` reads `block_table[src_col]` past the row width without a bounds check. Above the row width this is an illegal memory access (Xid 31, `FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ`); below it, the request silently restores the KDA/mamba state from an unrelated block.

**Where.**
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py`, `add_request`: `(new_req_data.num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size` (main, ~L70-77).
- `vllm/v1/engine/core.py`, `_initialize_kv_caches`: `vllm_config.cache_config.block_size = min(participating ...)` (main, ~L298-305). The comment there already notes that a small-block group "would otherwise drag the global block_size below the real allocator block size and desync it from mamba"; the min still includes any prefix-cacheable attention group with a smaller block.
- `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py`: `preprocess_mamba_align_fused_kernel` uses the seed as `src_col`; `_copy_mamba_state_block` loads `block_table_base + src_col` with no check against the row width. Mamba state blocks and the block-table row width (`cdiv(max_model_len, mamba_block_size) + num_speculative_blocks`) are in units of `mamba_block_size`.

#57699 describes a bug class for qwen3: when the model closes the tool call **without closing the last parameter tag**, the trailing value is dropped by the final (partial=False) conversion. #57707 fixes qwen3 only - but the same structure exists in three other converters, none of which are covered by that PR:

items.title: [RFC]: KV cache grouping for hybrid models with speculative drafters
items.bodyExcerpt:
**Status:** Draft · **PRs:** #58207 (group size), #58380 (prefer `BLHNC`, stacked on #58207)

## TL;DR

Speculative drafters on hybrid models add a small KV cache bucket of their own, which breaks vLLM's KV cache grouping heuristic in two ways:

- **Too many groups (Qwen3.5 / 3.6 + DFlash):** a one-layer drafter bucket forces **one group per layer**: Qwen3.5-27B goes from 4 to 70 groups (#49730), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B from 4 to 46. Each group rebuilds attention metadata every step, so DFlash loses much of its speedup; forcing fewer groups today costs KV cache capacity.
- **Full attention padding (MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash):** the 5-layer drafter bucket sets the group size, which doesn't divide the target's 9 full attention layers, so a full attention padding layer is allocated for the whole context (#58175). Kimi-K3 + DSpark has the same problem: its 5-layer drafter bucket pads the 24 MLA (full attention) layers, with 20 groups.

Checked and unaffected (identical grouping with and without these PRs): GLM-5.3-Flash + DFlash2, MiniMax-M3 + DSpark, DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark.

A two-part proposal fixes both:

| part | problem | fix | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash | MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1 · #58207** | small drafter buckets force per-layer KV groups, or full attn padding | pick the group size by worst-case padding **bytes**; `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (default 3) | 46 → **17** groups, **+54%** tok/s @c=1, **+36%** @c=32 | 11 → **7** groups, no full attn padding, KV capacity 5.76M → 5.96M |
| **2 · #58380** | `LBHNC` forces padding when drafter bytes/token ≠ target's | prefer `BLHNC` when the backends can run it and it avoids full attn padding or needs fewer groups | **5** groups, no padding, 7.53M tokens (> main's 7.42M); Triton only today | stays `LBHNC` at 7 groups (`BLHNC` would need 12 and has no full attn padding to remove) |

The parts are complementary: part 2 picks the path; part 1 is the fallback path (§5).

items.title: [Question][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer: does the 640-token block table reach 32-pool pages on gfx942/gfx950 too?
items.bodyExcerpt:
We found this on hardware vLLM doesn't support (gfx1030, Radeon Pro V620), running GLM-5.3-Flash without aiter. The code path involved is shared with gfx942/gfx950, and we have no MI300/MI355 to check it on. Could someone with one confirm or rule it out?

**What we see.** `Glm5NextIndexerCache` stores pooled keys in pages of 32 pools (storage block 128 tokens at `index_kpool=4`). The hybrid KDA page rule makes the attention block 640. On ROCm the sparse-MLA and indexer backends accept `MultipleOf(16)` (`get_supported_kernel_block_sizes`), so `select_common_block_size` keeps kernel block 640. The indexer metadata builder only converts the table when the storage block is a multiple of the kernel block (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`, prefill and decode branches; unchanged on main):

```python
if (
    kernel_block_size is not None
    and self.kv_cache_spec.block_size != kernel_block_size
    and self.kv_cache_spec.block_size % kernel_block_size == 0
):
    factor = self.kv_cache_spec.block_size // kernel_block_size
    indexer_block_table = (block_table[:, ::factor] // factor).contiguous()
```

128 % 640 ≠ 0, so the 640-token table goes to `get_compressed_slot_mapping` (the kpool writer) and to `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache_triton` as if each entry named one 32-pool page. With per-chunk block allocation:
- pools written before their block exists land in padding;
- positions past the allocated blocks alias block 0;
- positions past the 52-column table (at `max_model_len` 32768) are masked by the gather.

On NVIDIA the kernel block is 64, so the `// factor` branch applies. As far as we can tell nothing here is aiter-specific: the kpool path uses `forward_cuda` on ROCm whether aiter is on or off.

**Reproducer.** One GPU, stock vLLM only, no model: [`repro_rocm_kpool_table.py`](https://github.com/Omnicef/vllm/blob/glm53-v030/tests/local/repro_rocm_kpool_table.py). It writes a 9,432-token prompt in the served prefill chunks with the real ROCm kpool writer

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Add AITER MLA prefill kernel for dense MLA backend
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

Integrate AITER's `mla_prefill_fwd` assembly kernel into vLLM's dense MLA backend (`AiterMLAImpl`), replacing the base class's chunk-by-chunk prefill context path with a single kernel call that avoids expensive KV expansion.

### What this changes

The base class (`MLACommonImpl._compute_prefill_context`) computes context attention by:
1. Gathering cached KV per chunk
2. Expanding through `kv_b_proj` to materialize full K/V heads
3. Running `flash_attn_varlen` per chunk
4. Merging chunk results

This is expensive because `kv_b_proj` expansion materializes `O(context_len * num_heads * head_dim)` intermediate tensors.

The new path instead:
1. **Absorbs Q** through `W_UK^T` (extracted from `kv_b_proj` weights) to produce compressed queries in the latent space `[T, N, L+R]`
2. **Runs `mla_prefill_fwd`** directly against the paged KV cache in a single assembly kernel call — no KV expansion needed
3. **Projects output** through `W_UV` to recover full V dimensions

This eliminates the per-chunk KV expansion loop and replaces it with a single kernel dispatch.

### Fallback behavior

- **FP8 prefill**: Falls back to base class (AITER `mla_prefill_fwd` does not yet accept `q_scale`/`kv_scale`)
- **AITER unavailable**: Falls back to base class via `ImportError` guard

### Part of the GLM-5 on ROCm performance series

This PR is part of a series of optimizations to bring GLM-5 inference on ROCm (MI355X) closer to ATOM performance:

| PR | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|
| #38665 | Dual-stream shared experts + Quark MXFP4 + GLM-5-FP8 weight loading fix | Open |
| #36855 | Sparse MLA head repeat for < 16 heads + FP8 KV cache support | Open |
| **This PR** | MLA prefill kernel integration (eliminates KV expansion) | **New** |

Related upstream:
- [ROCm/aiter#2563](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/2563) — AITER sparse MLA ZeroDivisionError with < 16 heads
- [ROCm/aiter#2577](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/2577) — AITER

items.title: [Spec Decode] DFlash/DSpark draft support under decode context parallelism
items.bodyExcerpt:
### What

Make dense (GQA/MHA) DFlash/DSpark drafts work under `decode_context_parallel_size > 1`
by caching the whole DCP group's KV heads on every rank.

Rebased on `main` after #52188. That PR landed the DCP-aware draft slot mapping this
branch used to carry (`cp_local_slot` / `prepare_dcp_local_seq_lens` in
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cp_utils.py`), and its version is strictly better: it also handles
the null block and the rejected context suffix. That commit is dropped here in favour
of upstream's, leaving the part #52188 does not cover.

#52188 enables the MLA draft path (Kimi-K3, one latent KV head, no head-gather). This
PR enables the dense path, where the head-gather is exactly what breaks.

### Why (root cause)

Reported by @Leoyzen in #46514: DFlash/DSpark acceptance collapses to ~0% under DCP.

The dense flash DCP path (`_forward_with_dcp`: all-gather query heads across the DCP
group, attend against the rank-local KV shard, LSE-merge) is only correct when a rank's
KV shard holds the KV heads for all gathered query heads, i.e. KV heads replicated
across the DCP group. `verify_with_parallel_config` enforces this for dense *targets*;
nothing checked the *draft*. The GLM-5.2 DSpark draft is MHA (64q/64kv), so under TP4
each rank has a 16-head shard and the gathered 64 query heads are GQA-remapped 4:1 onto
the wrong KV heads.

### How

Cache the whole DCP group's KV heads on every rank (replicated) for that rank's
interleaved positions:

- `cache_num_kv_heads` decouples the KV-cache spec from the impl's head count
  (`Attention.__init__`, defaults to `num_kv_heads`, only larger for this case).
- The draft precompute all-gathers K/V across the DCP group in the same rank order the

items.bodyExcerpt:
Follow-up to #53808.

## Background

#53808 taught `get_merged_mm_kwargs` to overlay HF-style nested
`images_kwargs` / `videos_kwargs` / `audio_kwargs` onto the flat namespace, and
threaded a `modality` argument through Qwen2-VL and Qwen3-VL. Its docstring
states the rule:

> When `modality` is set, HF-style nested `images_kwargs` / `videos_kwargs` /
> `audio_kwargs` are overlaid onto the flat namespace for vLLM-side reads
> (token budgets, dummy inputs). Processor construction and HF `__call__`
> should omit `modality` so the nested dicts still reach the HF processor.

Every model outside the Qwen family that predicts sizes or token counts from
those kwargs was left reading the flat namespace only. The HF processor honors
the nested dict in its `__call__`, so vLLM and the processor disagree about how
many tokens an item expands to.

## Scope: every call site audited

Per review this now covers every multi-modal model, not just the VL three.
I enumerated every `get_merged_mm_kwargs` call site and classified each (40 when
this PR was opened, 44 on current `main`).

| `cohere_compass` | `_get_vision_info`, via `get_num_image_tokens` | threaded, as Qwen2-VL |

items.title: [Bugfix][GLM] Invalidate merged KDA convolution weights after refit
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55087.

GLM-5.3 KDA lazily merges the q/k/v convolution weights into a single cached tensor for the fused causal-conv path. During online RL or refit workflows, the underlying q/k/v convolution weights can be updated after warmup, but the derived merged tensor may remain stale. Subsequent inference can then continue using old or dummy weights even after the model weights have been refreshed.

This change:

- adds explicit invalidation for the merged KDA convolution-weight cache
- invalidates the KDA cache before GLM-5.3 model weight loading
- covers both the direct model-loading path and the top-level CausalLM loading path
- keeps the merged-weight cache for normal inference when weights are unchanged
- retains version/storage checks as additional protection against direct tensor mutations
- preserves the hot-path behavior by rebuilding only when needed

This PR is a follow-up to #53906, which introduced the GLM-5.3 implementation.

## Root cause

The KDA layer builds a single merged q|k|v convolution weight tensor and caches it in `_merged_conv_weight`. That cache was not always invalidated when the source q/k/v conv weights were replaced. In online-RL refit/update flows, this allowed stale merged weights to persist across reloads and be reused in later inference steps.

## Fix

- add invalidate_merged_conv_weight() / invalidate_kda_conv_weight_caches() methods to manually clear the stale cache
- invoke invalidation before every load_weights() call so refits always rebuild from fresh weights

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`hc_pre` / `hc_post` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/mhc.py` are rank-agnostic — they read `shape[-2:]` as `(hc_mult, hidden_size)` and treat everything before it as outer dims. The two helpers that feed them hardcode rank 2:

```python
def hc_expand(x, n):    return x.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n, -1).contiguous()
def hc_contract(x, n):  return x.mean(dim=1)
```


`hc_contract` has the matching problem: for rank-3 input, `mean(dim=1)` reduces over the token axis rather than the mHC axis.

Found while bringing up GLM-5.3-Flash on Intel Gaudi 2.

items.bodyExcerpt:
# [ROCm] HiSparse: host-resident sparse-MLA hot-buffering on gfx950

## Purpose

Enables HiSparse (#53781) on AMD ROCm, verified on gfx950 (MI350X, CDNA4).
HiSparse keeps the bulk of the sparse-MLA KV cache in pinned host memory and
pulls back only the indexer-selected rows just in time, so long-context agentic
sessions stop getting preempted. #53781 landed it CUDA-only.

## Changes

**Route HiSparse attention through the int64-safe Triton kernel.** HiSparse
points attention at a view over the *whole multi-layer KV slab*, so emitted row
indices scale with total block count: max row index is 33 off HiSparse and 7.5M
on. AITER's decode kernel computes `row_index * row_width` in int32, so on
GLM-5.3 (`row_width=576`) it wraps above row 3,728,270 and returns approximately
zero — no NaN, no assert. The Triton ragged path promotes the slot to
`tl.int64`, so under HiSparse it becomes unconditional, with
`allow_aiter_opus=False` so the prefill dispatcher cannot fall back into the
OPUS ASM kernel (same unverified addressing width). No flag, no env var.

**ROCm backend wiring.** CUDA HiSparse backends consume a dense `[tokens, topk]`
tensor; AITER's decode kernel consumes a ragged list plus indptr. Bridging that
is most of the diff: `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` registers with an
`index_group_builder` (which is what makes `mla_attention.py` pick up
`hisparse_cache`), decode converts dense physical top-k to ragged and attends
against the hot buffer, and prefill stages host rows via `stage_prefill_rows`
when the context is not fully resident. One new Triton kernel,
`compact_topk_to_ragged_triton` — `fetch_id_to_ragged_triton` was not reusable
because a mid-row `-1` must drop out rather than displace a valid entry.
AITER's persistent work-stealing metadata is disabled under HiSparse (its
buffers are sized in `build()`, but HiSparse rewrites the indptr at forward

items.title: kv-cache: honor scheduler lookahead in mamba align-mode allocation
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Problem

In mamba align cache mode (mamba-hybrid models with prefix caching), `MambaManager.allocate_new_blocks` and `get_num_blocks_to_allocate` discarded all lookahead tokens by resetting `num_tokens` to `num_tokens_main_model`. When the scheduler schedules lookahead capacity beyond a main-model sequence that ends exactly on a page boundary, this corrupts the recurrent state in two ways.

## Root cause

A mamba state table row is page-indexed: the worker's running-state column is `cdiv(main_end, bs) - 1`.

1. **Missing next page.** When a chunk ends exactly on a page boundary and lookahead tokens extend beyond it, the next page was not materialized with the current schedule. The boundary token's state write then targeted a block-table entry that still held a recycled stale block — the recurrent state is corrupted from that point on (one-step NaN followed by a repetition lock at every page boundary).

2. **Displaced running-state column.** If a page was materialized for the lookahead, the null padding was derived from the inflated `num_tokens`, so the reserved page displaced the real running-state column. The worker's running-state index (0 for a chunk ending at the first page boundary) pointed at the null slot; the next chunk's state pre-copy chained from the null slot and spec-decode acceptance collapsed to zero permanently for that request.

## Diagnosis

Reproduced on a 4-node Arm (Thor SM110) cluster serving GLM-5.3-Flash (mamba-hybrid + MTP + prefix caching) with deterministic single-turn probes: prompts whose prefill chunk ends exactly on a page boundary produced 0% spec-decode acceptance from the first decode step, while boundary-crossing-free prompts were healthy. The failure moved with cache layout across boots, and per-request scheduler dumps of the mamba state-table rows showed the displaced null column exactly at the worker's running-state index. The corruption was confirmed to chain through the state pre-copy (pre-copy source = the null slot).

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Cap the DynamicVideoBackend sampling fps
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`DynamicVideoBackend` (`vllm/multimodal/video.py`, registered as `opencv_dynamic`)
sizes its frame-candidate walk directly from the request-supplied `fps`, so the
amount of work is unbounded by anything in the video:

```python
fps = target.fps
...
if duration <= max_duration:
    n = int(math.floor(duration * fps))
    frame_indices_list = sorted(
        {min(max_frame_idx, math.ceil(i / fps * original_fps)) for i in range(n)}
    )
```

`n` scales with `fps`, but the *result* does not: the largest index reachable is
`duration * original_fps` regardless, and the set deduplicates at the end. So a
large `fps` buys nothing and costs CPU linearly.

This applies the same clamp the sibling backends in this file already use —
`_MAX_FPS: ClassVar[int] = 30` plus `fps = min(target.fps, cls._MAX_FPS)`, which
is verbatim what `QwenVLVideoBackend` (`:362`/`:373`, from the merged #56729) and
`GLMGAVideoBackend` (`:812`/`:839`) do.

## Reachability

`fps` is request-controlled through `media_io_kwargs`, and nothing strips it for
this backend:

1. `opencv_dynamic` is registered with `video_processor="Glm4vVideoProcessor"`,
   so it is the **default** backend on GLM-4V-family servers — a plain
   `POST /v1/chat/completions` with
   `"media_io_kwargs": {"video": {"fps": 100000}}` is enough, no override needed.
2. It registers with the default `requires_gpu=False`, so
   `VideoMediaIO.merge_kwargs` (`vllm/multimodal/media/video.py:60`) does **not**
   strip a request-level `video_backend: "opencv_dynamic"` either. The remaining
   `merge_kwargs` handling forwards `fps` verbatim.
3. It is also selected explicitly at
   `vllm/model_executor/models/nano_nemotron_vl.py:830`.

Only the `duration <= max_duration` branch is exposed. The `else` branch
self-bounds: `num_samples >= total_frames_num` short-circuits, and otherwise
`num_samples < total_frames_num`.

## Purpose

The existing kernel is implemented in pytorch and leads to **18** elementwise kernel launched per forward. We replace it with a single triton kernel.

GLM-5.3-Flash's indexer selects `topk + kpool_tail` tokens, where the tail size is <kpool=4 and depends on the number of tokens in the request. The persistent-topk kernel can miss higher-scoring entries, and the entries it misses depend on atomic ordering, so identical runs can differ.

## Purpose

Fix the sequence-parallel layout in the non-mHC branch of `Glm5NextDecoderLayer.forward()`.

`Glm5NextModel` shards tokens before entering decoder layers. The non-mHC branch passes that shard directly to attention without gathering the full sequence or reduce-scattering its output. items.title: [Kernel] Bump FlashKDA to keep the recurrent state in fp32
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Bumps the FlashKDA pin from `b59532f` to `17a037d`, the merge of vllm-project/FlashKDA#13 on its `dev` branch.

Before this change, FlashKDA's K2 kernel stored the KDA recurrent state in bf16 and rounded it after every 16-token tile. On long GLM-5.3-Flash prefills the error builds up across tiles and across chunked-prefill boundaries, and it shows up as corrupted long-context tool-call output. FlashKDA#13 keeps the state in fp32 between tiles, adds missing TMA store waits, and fixes a register-pressure regression on sm_10x.

The only change is the one-line `GIT_TAG` in `cmake/external_projects/flashkda.cmake`. FlashKDA's op schema, `flash_kda.h`, source file list and cutlass submodule are the same at both commits.

Not a duplicate: no other change to the FlashKDA pin is on main since #12, and I found no open PR bumping it.

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Parse split GLM tool-call markers
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #58315.

GLM required-tool grammar can emit `<tool_call>` and `</tool_call>` as ordinary sub-token sequences, while the streaming parser recognizes only their dedicated token IDs. In required-tool mode this mismatch can leave a valid tool call in the response content. This change lets the GLM parser opt into the textual marker forms after the actual reasoning-end token boundary, including the adapter path that skips reasoning parsing. Other parsers and automatic tool choice keep their existing behavior.

I checked the issue comments and searched open PRs by issue number and GLM/parser area. No open PR addresses this split-marker grammar/parser mismatch. The related GLM parser PRs address different grammar and argument parsing cases.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/parser/engine tests/parser/test_parse.py tests/parser/test_streaming.py -q`
- Ruff check and format checks on the changed Python files
- `git diff --check`

## Test Result

- Parser suites: **4,775 passed**, 14 existing PyTorch deprecation warnings.
- Ruff checks/format and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Model inference evaluation: not run. The regression tests exercise the captured GLM-5 split-marker stream and atomic marker-token cases directly through the parser; no target model was loaded in this environment.

AI assistance was used to develop and validate this change. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and approved the contribution.
